top.title: Julian Hall’s USMNT Future Hinges On One Game
top.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The clock is ticking for Julian Hall. The 18-year-old Red Bulls star has a clear path to lock in his future with the USMNT, but it comes with a catch. If Hall steps onto the pitch for the United States in the upcoming Concacaf Nations League matches against Haiti, he will be permanently tied to the American side under FIFA rules. This means no going back to Poland, his other eligible nation through his mother’s heritage. USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino believes the young talent is ready . He told reporters Wednesday that Hall “fully deserves” the call-up after his performances in the previous window. He added that he did not hear Hall’s earlier comments about Poland, but that when Hall was with the team he “was really excited to play for us, for USA. That’s what is important.” The coach emphasized that commitment and performance matter more than past statements. The Rules of the Tie FIFA rules make the distinction clear for players under 21. An appearance in any official competition permanently ties a player to that national team, while friendlies alone do not. Hall has four senior caps so far, all in friendlies, so he is not yet locked in. The upcoming matches against Haiti count as official competition under CONCACAF and FIFA. Miami hosts the first match on Nov. 14, while the second occurs in Cincinnati on Nov. 17. If Hall plays in either of these, the door to Poland slams shut. He would need to file a one-time switch request, which is only possible if he hasn’t played in an official senior game yet. The window to change his mind is closing fast. A Talent Worth the Risk Pochettino is not taking chances with his roster. He brought in a wave of teenagers to test them in friendlies earlier this year, and the results were loud. During the international break spanning September and October, Hall netted three goals and recorded one assist. He earned his first senior call-up then and proved he could handle the pace. The coach sees this as a chance to blend youth with experience. Wednesday, during a video conference with reporters, Pochettino said “It’s a great opportunity,” “to mix younger [players] with experienced players.” The mix includes veterans like Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun, who are back after missing the friendly run. Hall fits right in with that new energy. Poland Still in the Mix? Back in September, Hall did not rule out the Polish national team. He told the New York Post that his international future was “definitely not solidified for me” before his first USMNT camp. He was clear about his feelings then. “I appreciate the opportunity, and I’m going to do as much as I can to make an impact, but I’m definitely still open to my Polish side,” he said. top.description: …warns against using courts to cripple opposition By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has warned the All Progressives Congress (APC) against setting Nigeria on fire in its desperation to retain power in 2027, accusing the ruling party of using the judiciary to cripple the opposition and undermine democratic competition. The party issued the warning after a Federal High Court judgment in Abuja which it said threatens its leadership and the candidacy of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar. It argued that the implications extend beyond its leadership, potentially affecting thousands of candidates seeking elective offices across the country. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC linked the timing of the judgment by Justice Peter Lifu, barely 24 hours after its massive presidential campaign rally in Sokoto, to what it described as the APC’s growing desperation over the opposition’s rising political profile. “We have reasons to believe that the judgment had long been written on this case. The Sokoto rally was simply a trigger that stampeded its delivery,” Abdullahi alleged. The party warned that the dispute was not merely about the political fortunes of Senator David Mark or Atiku, but the right of its candidates to participate in the 2027 elections. “Do these people understand what they are playing with? This is not about Atiku Abubakar or David Mark. It is about the democratic rights of Nigerians to freely choose their own leaders. It is about the rights of thousands of candidates to participate in a democratic process,” the statement said. To challenge the judgment, the ADC cited an earlier ruling by Justice Musa Liman of the same Federal High Court, delivered on July 2, 2026, in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1637/2025, which it said affirmed the legitimacy of the David Mark-led National Working Committee (NWC) and directed the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise the leadership. The party argued that a court of coordinate jurisdiction could not sit on appeal over, review, vary or nullify a subsisting judgment of another court of equal jurisdiction. “The ADC, therefore, rejects any consequential orders founded on a determination that appears to disregard these fundamental legal principles. However, we await the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the said judgment to ascertain its precise terms, scope and operative orders,” Abdullahi stated. The ADC accused the APC of repeating what it called a familiar pattern of using judicial controversies to frustrate opposition whenever it gains political momentum, warning that the struggle to retain power must not come at the expense of national stability. “We warn the APC: do not play with fires you cannot control. top.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s five great moments with Portugal
top.description: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday to bring down the curtain on more than two decades in the Portugal shirt. He scored a record 146 times in a mammoth 234 appearances for his country having made his debut in 2003. Here are his five stand-out games with the Selecao. 2013: Outclassing Zlatan Having won the World Cup play-off first leg 1-0 against Sweden thanks to the iconic No. 7, Portugal headed to Stockholm for the return fixture. Ronaldo opened the scoring before Zlatan Ibrahimovic brought the sides level in the tie with a double in the Swedish capital. But the then Real Madrid attacker claimed Portugal’s spot at the tournament in Brazil by completing his hat-trick in two minutes. 2016: Tears before the joy Portugal reached the Euro 2016 final having failed to win a single group game. Ronaldo’s side went into the decider against hosts France in Paris searching for their first major international trophy and to make up for the past after losing to Greece on home soil 12 years earlier. The forward left the field injured and in tears after just 25 minutes before spending the rest of the game on the touchline cheering on his teammates. Eder scored the winner in extra-time to the relief of Ronaldo and 11 million Portuguese compatriots. 2018: One-man mission Fresh from winning three straight Champions Leagues with Real, Ronaldo faced Spain in Portugal’s World Cup opener in 2018. CR7 opened the scoring in Sochi with a penalty before grabbing a hat-trick, including a superb late free kick, to fire Portugal to a thrilling draw. 2025: 40 years young Three months after turning 40, Ronaldo helped Portugal to the Nations League final against Spain in Munich. He scored the winner over Germany in the semi-final before claiming the equaliser against Spain to send the decider to extra time. The Selecao eventually won on penalties, six years on from winning the same crown. 2026: Outplayed Croatia Following a lacklustre group stage, Ronaldo and Portugal faced Croatia in the last 32 of this year’s World Cup in Toronto. Despite the prospect of it being his final ever World Cup match, Ronaldo took control of things. He had an early effort chalked off for offside and Ivan Perisic put Croatia ahead, but Ronaldo equalised for Portugal from the penalty spot. Goncalo Ramos’ late header gave Portugal a memorable 2-1 victory and sent them into the last 16, where they lost to eventual winners Spain. top.title: Indiana Fever make another cut as front-office shake-up continues
top.description: Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indiana Fever’s front-office overhaul isn’t slowing down, with the franchise quietly cutting ties with another figure. Indiana’s front-office reset has turned into pure chaos this offseason. With Kelly Krauskopf stepping down and Amber Cox shown the door, the Fever are scrambling to find a general manager while deciding against hiring a president of basketball operations. Sophie Cunningham remains a free agent, while Kelsey Mitchell just delivered an All-WNBA year alongside Caitlin Clark, but even her future is up in the air, as she also enters free agency. And it doesn’t look as if the shake-up is complete yet when it comes to the front office, as there’s been another departure behind the scenes. According to IX Sports , the Fever have moved on from basketball operations and equipment manager Kristin Moore. Kristin Moore arrived in Indiana back in early 2025 after running equipment for the Las Vegas Aces and Stanford, quickly climbing from operations coordinator to basketball ops manager. But her quiet exit after nearly two years just throws more fuel on the fire surrounding Stephanie White. Despite steering the Fever into the postseason, White’s grace period with the fanbase has evaporated, with a loud corner of the market calling for a fresh voice. The outside noise isn’t helping either, with chatter loosely floating her name for the vacant Liberty gig after Chris DeMarco got fired. top.title: Xavier soccer eyes state title with simple strategy
top.description: The Xavier boys soccer team has what seems like a pretty simple strategy. The Hawks figure if you don’t have the ball, you can’t score. It’s a high-level game of keep-away that has been effective for the Hawks, who have qualified for the WIAA state tournament for the first time since 2012. “I feel like as long as we have the ball, we have control of the game,” said senior midfielder Mauricio Laguna-Ramirez, who leads the Hawks with 15 assists. “I think that’s really what we try to do. We try to control the game, try to keep the ball as much as possible because at the end of the day, if the other team doesn’t have the ball, they don’t have any chances to score.” Xavier (14-7) is the No. 4 seed in the Division 4 semifinals and will play No. 1 seed Lake Country Lutheran (16-1-2) at 11 a.m. on Friday, Nov. 6, at Uihlein Soccer Park in Milwaukee. The Hawks are making their sixth trip to WIAA state and have been successful in their previous five appearances at state with four titles and an 8-1 all-time record. Their state titles came in Division 2 in 2003, 2004, 2006 and 2012. The Hawks have been painfully close to the state tournament in recent seasons only to fall short. They lost to Sturgeon Bay in a shootout in the sectional final last season and lost to St. Mary Catholic in the sectional final in 2023. “It’s a great accomplishment,” said junior midfielder Ethan Sharkey, who leads the Hawks with 17 goals and 35 points. “Obviously, last year, we lost in the sectional final. It’s a great opportunity that we can progress further than that. I feel like we have a great core group. We have great people coming off the bench, and I feel like we can make a run at the title this year.” Xavier has won four matches in a row and eight of its last nine after a 4-2 sectional final win over Providence Academy on Oct. 31. top.title: Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons gets brutally honest on expectations when he returns to play after ACL injury
top.description: The Green Bay Packers are in last place in the NFC North despite having a 5-3 record. They have the best record of any last place team through eight weeks in the NFL since 1970, which is a testament to how well the division has played up to this point in the season. Truth be told, though, the Packers would be in a better position if they were not just 1-2 against their division opponents thus far in 2026. As the season hits its midway point and the weather becomes cold, Green Bay is going to be looking at making a run at a postseason spot. Fortunately, they will have All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons back soon, though he himself told fans to temper their expectations a little bit. Green Bay Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons needs to get back into game shape Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) during a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 12, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers defeated the Bengals 27-18. Parsons, of course, has not played yet this season as he continues to recover from the torn ACL he suffered late last year. When he first went down, the All-Pro prematurely predicted a September return. Now, we are in November and he has yet to play. This, however, is not because of any setbacks. The fact of the matter is that Parsons tore his meniscus as well. Furthermore, the Packers do not want him back on the field until he is 100% and has no risk of reinjuring that knee (remember what happened to David Bakhtiari?) While this is understood by most, it is easy to fall into the trap of thinking that Parsons will immediately be in mid-season form the second he steps onto the field for the first time. He himself told reporters that will not be the case. “I had a full lateral and medial meniscus repair, including the ACL, so when people are walking at three weeks, I’m still not weight bearing, so my quad is fully dead,” Parsons said . “I didn’t get off crutches until seven to eight weeks. So if you count that two months, I’m exactly where a nine-month (recovery) is supposed to be. So that’s why everyone’s timelines are different. I had a lot of damage done to my leg, and I think it’s a miracle that I’m even standing here today and opening up my window this early. “Am I going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person that I once was, this year? Probably not until later. I think you’ll see flashes of All-Pro Micah when I get to pass rush, and there’s gonna be times when you’re gonna be like, ‘Dang, what was Micah doing?’ There’s gonna be times that I question myself, too, like, ‘What was I doing right there?’… I’m not shying away from the possibility of my bad plays.” Fortunately, Green Bay’s pass rush has been better than many thought it would be without their All-Pro. Lukas Van Ness, Brenton Cox, Dani Dennis-Sutton, and others along the defensive front have picked up the slack and have the Packers tied for sixth in the NFL for most team sacks. top.title: Thursday Cannon Fodder: creeping
top.description: 03 November 2026, Thuringia, Erfurt: A heavy-duty crane is being used to lift a fir tree off a truck. A Canadian coastal fir has been erected on Erfurt's Domplatz, where it will serve as this year's large Christmas tree. The tree came from a private property in Oberhof and had been cut down on November 2 for traffic safety reasons. Its installation marked the start of the visible setup phase for the 176th Erfurt Christmas Market. Photo: Jacob Schröter/dpa (Photo by Jacob Schröter/picture alliance via Getty Images) Good Thursday morning, TSFers! Once again, it’s almost the weekend and that is always cause for celebration. It’s been a busy few weeks in my household with celebrations and guests, which is lovely, but we’ve got very little on the schedule for Saturday and Sunday and I’m thrilled. Speaking of celebrations, apparently it’s time to get ready for Christmas. At least according to Arsenal! To be fair, it’s an excellent video. I’m certain that as I watch it again, I’ll notice more references to last season and the celebrations. Colin Firth, who I think I knew supports the club, doing a nod to his Love Actually performance is fun, too. But c’mon, folks. It’s November 5th (remember, remember). There are 49 days until Christmas. The Christmas candy should not be on display in the grocery store (it’s on display in my grocery store). The Halloween decorations are still up on some of the houses in the neighborhood (like mine) and the garland and wreaths are going up. The holiday creep is too much! And I say that as someone who really enjoys the holiday time. As I write that, I remember that just because it isn’t for me doesn’t mean it isn’t for everybody. Don’t yuck someone else’s yum, Aaron. If I had my way, we’d wait a bit longer to pivot towards Christmas, but if you’re ready, go right ahead!

top.title: 4 key matchups to watch in Bengals vs. Falcons
top.description: The Cincinnati Bengals will be playing the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid, Spain, this week. The Bengals are coming off a 43-36 victory against the Tennessee Titans, while the Falcons lost 16-0 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Buccaneers did not complete a pass during the game, and yet still won by double digits in a rain-soaked contest. Even with that loss this past week, the 3-5 Falcons are not a team to take lightly. They have victories over the Packers, Saints, and the 49ers this season. They also have one-score losses against the Steelers, Ravens, and Bears. They will be getting back their best pass rusher, James Pearce Jr., this week also. He is coming off an 8-game suspension he served for violating the NFL’s conduct policy. Orlando Brown Jr. vs. James Pearce Jr. With the aforementioned Pearce coming off of his suspension, he is listed as the starter at right outside linebacker in the Falcons’ 3-4 defense. That means he is likely to face off against Orlando Brown Jr. this week. Brown struggled at times on Sunday when faced off against the speedier pass rush of Jacob Martin. He will see a similar test with the athletic Pearce this week. Orlando Brown Jr. allowed a season-high 6 pressures versus Tennessee. He was also credited with allowing a sack. Brown will have to play much better this week against Pearce. Last season Pearce produced at an elite level for a rookie. He finished the season with 45 pressures and 10.5 sacks for the Falcons. The Bengals will need to keep Pearce and the rest of a dynamic Falcons pass rush in check this week. While it will be up to everyone to try and limit him this week, I am specifically curious to see how Barrett Carter, Demetrius Knight Jr., and Jordan Battle play. Those three players have struggled with missed tackles the last couple of seasons. Robinson is one of the most dynamic and elusive running backs in the league. He can make guys look absolutely silly out in space, and that trio will have to play sound football. If they don’t, we are going to see them all over the Bijan Robinson highlight reel. top.title: The one Portugal milestone Cristiano Ronaldo failed to reach as he announces retirement
top.description: Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images Cristiano Ronaldo is arguably the greatest soccer player to ever play for Portugal and has helped the national team win three trophies during his 23-year career. Despite having helped the nation reach heights they were not used to reaching, Ronaldo fell short of one achievement, which he always wanted to achieve with Portugal, and that was making 250 appearances. As he announced his retirement today, Ronaldo walks away with 234 international appearances and 146 goals, the most by any player. The announcement comes just one month after he left the Portuguese football camp in September, following controversy with head coach Jorge Jesus. “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team,” Ronaldo said in an Instagram video. “Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone – they are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.” The Portuguese national team put out an official video on Instagram with a powerful caption that read: “A legacy that will live on forever. Thank you for everything, captain.” They also put out a statement to inform fans that a tribute was in the works for the legendary soccer player. “It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo’s immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much,” the statement read. Throughout his career, Ronaldo represented Portugal in six European Championships and won the competition once in 2016. He has also played in six World Cups and led the national team to the semi-finals in 2006. Ronaldo played in 178 competitive games and 56 friendlies throughout his career. 57 of his competitive appearances came in the World Cup and Euros. The 41-year-old has scored 25 goals in these games and helped his country become one of the leading nations in soccer. As he retires from international football, the country will now be without an icon who has carried the expectations of the Portuguese people for over two decades. Although many would say that his performances declined in the past few years, there was still an expectation of something big happening with him on the field. However, with the legend now having announced his retirement, the next generation of Portuguese talent will have to showcase that they are capable of taking the country to great heights. top.title: Rare freshman starter Tommy Tofi settling in along Oregon football OL
top.description: It's been a bumpy ride for Oregon football's first regular-season true freshman starter in the Dan Lanning era. From the onset, Tommy Tofi, at a massive 6-foot-6, 360 pounds, possessed the tools to succeed in his first year with the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten). Still, Lanning and offensive line coach A'lique Terry rarely go to first-year players along the interior. The only other first-year player to start for the Ducks under Lanning was current starting center Iapani Laloulu, who started the 2023 Fiesta Bowl only because Jackson Powers-Johnson opted out of the game. This is rare territory for an Oregon offensive lineman ahead of the Ducks ' biggest game of the season versus Ohio State. "It’s all been like kinda crazy," Tofi said. "Trying out different positions from left to right and just finding my rhythm." Tofi was used sparingly over the first month of the season and struggled with his assignments at times when he did get on the field. The freshman hasn't had trouble moving opposing players and creating gaps when he finds the right body, but the key has been being assignment sound. Since the second half against Nebraska on Oct. 17, Tofi has firmly held on to the left guard spot along the offensive line. He started his first game the week after against Illinois and played his best game of the season versus Northwestern last week. He said playing between Laloulu at center and veteran tackle Fox Crader has been instrumental to his success, along with his fair share of "cuss-outs." "A lot of cuss-outs from (Laloulu), (Douglas Utu) and a lot of the players," Tofi said with a smile when asked about how he's developed. "When you have four first-rounders on that D-line, that’s what helps you prepare and gets you ready for the season. Being able to go head-up with Matayo (Uiagalelei), Bear (Alexander), A’Mauri (Washington), Teitum (Tuioti), iron sharpens iron. You get better and better every day." Tofi has been part of a much-improved offensive line group that has stuck with a consistent group for the first time this season after rotating through different lineups over the first month and a half of the season. Ultimately, Lanning still wants to see more "strain" and effort from Tofi when the situation requires it. "Tommy is a guy that we’ve had a lot of confidence in from the beginning," Lanning said. "He’s got really good strength, got the ability to move people, which is huge. Now it’s about finding that extra strain. Can I strain from every play? I feel like every week that’s gotten a little better for Tommy." Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard. You may reach him at adietz@registerguard.com . Want to see more Oregon Ducks coverage? Subscribe to The Register-Guard’s newsletter . nigeria.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s five great moments with Portugal
nigeria.description: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football on Thursday to bring down the curtain on more than two decades in the Portugal shirt. He scored a record 146 times in a mammoth 234 appearances for his country having made his debut in 2003. Here are his five stand-out games with the Selecao. 2013: Outclassing Zlatan Having won the World Cup play-off first leg 1-0 against Sweden thanks to the iconic No. 7, Portugal headed to Stockholm for the return fixture. Ronaldo opened the scoring before Zlatan Ibrahimovic brought the sides level in the tie with a double in the Swedish capital. But the then Real Madrid attacker claimed Portugal’s spot at the tournament in Brazil by completing his hat-trick in two minutes. 2016: Tears before the joy Portugal reached the Euro 2016 final having failed to win a single group game. Ronaldo’s side went into the decider against hosts France in Paris searching for their first major international trophy and to make up for the past after losing to Greece on home soil 12 years earlier. The forward left the field injured and in tears after just 25 minutes before spending the rest of the game on the touchline cheering on his teammates. Eder scored the winner in extra-time to the relief of Ronaldo and 11 million Portuguese compatriots. 2018: One-man mission Fresh from winning three straight Champions Leagues with Real, Ronaldo faced Spain in Portugal’s World Cup opener in 2018. CR7 opened the scoring in Sochi with a penalty before grabbing a hat-trick, including a superb late free kick, to fire Portugal to a thrilling draw. 2025: 40 years young Three months after turning 40, Ronaldo helped Portugal to the Nations League final against Spain in Munich. He scored the winner over Germany in the semi-final before claiming the equaliser against Spain to send the decider to extra time. The Selecao eventually won on penalties, six years on from winning the same crown. 2026: Outplayed Croatia Following a lacklustre group stage, Ronaldo and Portugal faced Croatia in the last 32 of this year’s World Cup in Toronto. Despite the prospect of it being his final ever World Cup match, Ronaldo took control of things. He had an early effort chalked off for offside and Ivan Perisic put Croatia ahead, but Ronaldo equalised for Portugal from the penalty spot. Goncalo Ramos’ late header gave Portugal a memorable 2-1 victory and sent them into the last 16, where they lost to eventual winners Spain. nigeria.title: Bank of England Lifts Rate For First Time Since 2023 To Fight Inflation
nigeria.description: The Bank of England raised its benchmark interest rate to four percent on Thursday, the first increase in more than three years, as soaring energy costs push up global inflation. The central bank tightened borrowing costs by a quarter point, catching up with the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank in lifting rates since the start of the Middle East conflict. Along with Ukraine’s strikes on Russian refineries, disruptions to Gulf energy supplies owing to the US-Iran war have caused record-high diesel prices around the world. “There is now enough inflationary pressure in the pipeline caused by the rise in energy prices, that an increase in Bank Rate is warranted,” BoE governor Andrew Bailey said in a statement. “Today’s increase shouldn’t be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes,” Bailey said. “But, unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase.” Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey attends the Bank of England Monetary Policy Report press conference at Bank Of England in London on November 5, 2026. Photo by ALISHIA ABODUNDE / POOL / AFP Despite surging inflation, the bank upgraded its forecasts for UK economic growth in 2026 and 2027. The central bank now estimates gross domestic product to hit 1.6 percent this year and 1.3 percent next year. In July, it had forecast GDP output of 1.1 percent in both years. The BoE last raised its key interest rate in August 2023, and has kept the cost of borrowing at 3.75 percent since December. Britain’s annual inflation rate accelerated by more than expected in September, rising to 3.5 percent — well above the bank’s target of two percent. The BoE on Thursday said its central forecast saw UK inflation peaking at 4.9 in the second quarter of next year. Millions of Britons face a jump in energy bills from the start of next year, even after the government offered some assistance in its annual budget announcement last week. nigeria.title: Troops rescue nine kidnapped victims, recover 108 livestock in Kebbi
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued nine kidnapped victims and recovered 108 livestock during security operations in Danko general area and Sabon Tunga and Binoni villages in Danko-Wasagu Local Government Area of Kebbi State. nigeria.title: I now take English classes to speak fluently – MC Oluomo
nigeria.description: The President of the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW), Musiliu Akinsanya, popularly known as MC Oluomo, has disclosed that he is taking English lessons to improve his spoken communication. The transport union leader made this known while addressing Nollywood actor Adams Kehinde, popularly known as Lege Miami, and other attendees at a rally organised in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Speaking in Yoruba, MC Oluomo admitted that he and Lege Miami were not fluent in English, revealing that he had enrolled for lessons to improve his proficiency in the language. He also noted that despite travelling frequently to different countries, he had yet to become fluent in spoken English. “Neither of us speaks English fluently, so I am taking classes to improve. I travel around the world. I am a citizen of America,” he said. MC Oluomo further spoke about his children’s educational and professional achievements in the United States, noting that they were more proficient in English than he was. “My children can speak better than me. My children in the US are nurses, a doctor and an engineer,” he added. He explained that he sometimes handed the microphone to his children to speak on his behalf whenever he struggled to express himself in English. The disclosure comes amid previous public criticism of his spoken English, particularly in April 2025, when a video of him pronouncing the word “kudos” as “kundusi” while addressing union members in Abuja went viral. Responding to the criticism at the time, MC Oluomo acknowledged his limitations in the English language but maintained that fluency in the language did not determine one’s achievements. “Grammar won’t finish Nigeria. I might not understand the English language, but I understand Yoruba,” he said. nigeria.title: France workers strike, march for ‘dignified wage’
nigeria.description: Striking workers marched across France against the rising cost of living on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands of people expected to take to the streets nationwide in a new escalation following weeks of protest. The demonstrations come as the eurozone’s second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls. The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years. Sylvie Larneury, 61, a healthcare manager, and her 61-year-old partner, an IT specialist, were on strike Thursday so they could join the march in the central city of Clermont-Ferrand. “We’re fed up. We’re not starving, but we have to help our children even though they’ve studied,” she said. “We’ve had enough of social injustice,” she added, criticising what she called “a repressive government that defends its own interests and not those of the majority”. nigeria.title: Eisenkot tipped to seek Israel government as religious party drops Netanyahu
nigeria.description: Gadi Eisenkot emerged on Thursday as the favourite to be tasked with trying to form an Israeli government as a religious party long aligned with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declined to recommend him. President Isaac Herzog was holding a second day of consultations with political parties after the October 27 election, in which neither Netanyahu — a polarising right-winger who has led Israel through three years of war — nor Eisenkot — a former military chief promising to restore national unity — secured enough votes for a majority. Herzog will choose by himself whom to ask to form a new government but traditionally the mandate is given to the person recommended by more parties, which would be Eisenkot. The opposition leader also received a recommendation from a key lawmaker from the Israeli-Arab minority, whose seats in parliament soared due to outrage over Netanyahu’s policies, even as Eisenkot has remained unclear on whether he would accept Arab support to form a government. United Torah Judaism, which backed Netanyahu after the previous five elections, in its meeting with Herzog declined to recommend Netanyahu again as prime minister, although it also did not side with Eisenkot. The party informed Herzog “that it has decided not to recommend any member of Knesset to form a government,” the president’s office said in a statement, referring to the 120-member parliament in which United Torah Judaism has won seven seats. The party — which represents ultra-Orthodox Jews of Ashkenazi origin, who mostly hail from or have roots in Europe — as well as Shas — which represents the same community but of Sephardic, or mostly Middle Eastern and North African descent — have both been backed by Netanyahu as they push to maintain the exemption from military service for religious students. Netanyahu has preserved the exemption but stopped short of enshrining it in law, in the face of major resentment from many other Israelis as reservists serve multiple tours due to the wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. “In whatever government is next formed, our immediate item is sorting out the status of Torah students,” United Torah Judaism lawmaker Isaac Pindrus said. Eisenkot, who has tried to appeal to secular Israelis from left to right, has been adamant about closing exemptions to military service. Some of his opposition allies have criticised the ultra-Orthodox, who make up about 14 percent of the population but have far higher birthrates than secular Israelis, as a drain on the state. Observers say United Torah Judaism’s tactic is likely aimed mostly at punishing Netanyahu and showing that their votes cannot be taken for granted, while they would still serve in a government if he were to form one. – Arab-Israelis play key role – Once Herzog gives his mandate to a lawmaker, the person — presumably either Eisenkot or Netanyahu — will have 28 days to form a government, with a potential 14-day extension. The group described the call as a politically motivated attempt to undermine the lawmaker ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday, its President, Abdullahi Omeiza, said the group was concerned about what it described as the growing tendency among political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric for partisan purposes. He said: “We are concerned about the growing tendency among some political actors to deploy anti-corruption institutions and rhetoric as instruments of partisan warfare. “Accountability is important, but it must be pursued through facts, evidence and established legal procedures, not through sensational political narratives designed to damage the reputation of an elected public official.” The group argued that constituency empowerment programmes should not automatically be classified as vote-buying simply because they involve direct financial assistance to beneficiaries. It said such initiatives could be subjected to legitimate scrutiny, but insisted that any investigation must be guided by evidence and the law. “The mere distribution of financial assistance to constituents does not, in itself, establish an offence of vote-buying,” the statement added. On the demand for an EFCC investigation and prosecution, the group acknowledged that no one was above the law but cautioned against turning anti-corruption agencies into instruments of political intimidation. Omeiza said: “Accountability is indispensable to democratic governance, but it must never become a convenient weapon for settling political scores. “Allegations are not convictions, petitions are not proof of wrongdoing, and public accusations cannot substitute for due process. “The EFCC must be allowed to discharge its statutory responsibilities independently, without being subjected to political pressure or media-driven prejudgement.” The group challenged the Obi-Kwankwaso Movement to submit any credible evidence to the appropriate authorities rather than rely on public declarations and what it described as inflammatory narratives. It also maintained that the people of Kogi Central had the right to assess Akpoti-Uduaghan’s performance and determine whether she deserved another term. “The people of Kogi Central are politically conscious, discerning and capable of evaluating their representative. nigeria.title: UK to hold talks on harms of slave trade
nigeria.description: Commonwealth leaders have welcomed Britain’s agreement to engage in “time-bound inclusive and good-faith dialogue” over the “historical harms” of the transatlantic slave trade. In a final communique issued late on Wednesday, the group of nations said the time had come for “meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation towards forging a common future based on equity”. But it did not set out a timetable for the talks. It comes after British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to saying sorry but ruled out paying financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries. Burnham used his appearance at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda to hold discussions about issuing a formal apology for Britain’s role in slavery, which saw about 10-15 million slaves brought from Africa to the Americas over four centuries. In a speech to opening the biannual Commonwealth leaders meeting on Tuesday, King Charles III, who is politically neutral, called the slave trade “a monstrous injustice” that filled him with “profound personal sorrow”, stopping short of a formal apology. Britain’s pivotal part in slavery has long strained relations between the UK and its former colonies, including an awkward previous meeting of Commonwealth leaders in 2024. “We welcome the agreement of the government of the United Kingdom to engage in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms,” the final communique said. The Commonwealth is a 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies. Of those Charles remains head of state in 14. Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said it is “not feasible” for the country to pay reparations for slavery, but that “there are things we can work on co-operatively”. Miliband also hinted that Britain could issue a formal apology next year when it hosts a G20 leaders’ summit, in comments to the BBC aired on Wednesday as the meeting wrapped up. nigeria.title: Kane becomes highest-paid footballer in Europe after new deal
nigeria.description: England captain Harry Kane has signed a record-breaking contract extension with Bayern Munich that will keep him at the German club until June 2029, in a deal reportedly making him the highest-paid player in Europe by basic salary. According to David Ornstein of The Athletic , the three-year extension is the most lucrative contract in Bayern Munich’s history, although some European players could still earn more than the striker when performance-related bonuses are included. The 33-year-old’s previous contract was due to expire next summer, but both Kane and the Bundesliga champions were keen to continue their partnership. Bayern reportedly do not consider the new agreement his final contract, with the club keen to retain the England international for the foreseeable future. Speaking after signing the extension, Kane expressed his satisfaction with life in Munich, describing his relationship with the club, supporters and city as a special one. “I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich,” he said. “We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. “I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.” The contract extension comes after a remarkable period for the striker, who won the Ballon d’Or in late October, becoming the first English player to receive the prestigious award since 2001. He is also expected to become England’s most-capped player during the November international break. Since joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur three years ago, Kane has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances, establishing himself as one of the club’s most influential players. During his time in Germany, he has won two Bundesliga titles, the DFB-Pokal and two Supercups. However, winning the UEFA Champions League remains a major ambition for the England captain as he looks to add Europe’s biggest club competition to his collection of honours. His decision to extend his stay in Germany also appears to have dealt a significant blow to hopes of him returning to the Premier League to challenge Alan Shearer’s all-time scoring record. With his Bayern future secured until 2029, Kane looks increasingly likely to prioritise further success in Germany over a return to English football. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone— they are also made with the heart. “A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end,” he added. Forty-one-year-old Ronaldo, who currently plays club football at Al Nassr, scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for his country since his debut in 2003. Portugal’s forward Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates scoring his team’s second goal during the 2026 World Cup qualifiers Europe zone group F football match between Portugal and Hungary at Jose Alvalade stadium in Lisbon on October 14, 2025. The forward’s announced his retirement weeks after he walked out of the Portugal camp last month, following news that he would not be in the starting line-up in the Nations League match against Denmark. In October, he fell out with national coach Jorge Jesus after he refused to play him in a Nations League match. Ronaldo immediately left the team camp and was handed a 30-day suspension. Throughout his international career, Ronaldo won the European Championship with Portugal in 2016 in France, although he had to leave the field during the final due to an injury. business.title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine American Bitcoin (ABTC) Posts $126 Million Profit as Holdings Gain $197 Million American Bitcoin Corp. (Nasdaq: ABTC) reported about $126 million in third-quarter net income on Wednesday, a swing from a $57.2 million loss in the prior quarter that rested largely on a $197.3 million gain on the company’s bitcoin holdings rather than on mining revenue. The Miami-based miner and treasury company, a majority-owned subsidiary of Hut 8 Corp. and co-founded with Trump family backing, mined about 891 bitcoin in the quarter at a cost of roughly $42,100 each and ended September with about 8,427 BTC. Mining revenue was about $63.4 million, down from about $67.0 million in the second quarter. Gross profit was about $25.8 million, a 41% margin, compared with about $33.0 million and 49% a quarter earlier, as seasonal power costs rose across its sites. Adjusted EBITDA came in at about $221 million, compared with an Adjusted EBITDA loss of about $45.0 million in the second quarter, according to the company’s release . Eric Trump, co-founder and chief strategy officer of American Bitcoin, said the quarter delivered the net income and Adjusted EBITDA figures while growing the bitcoin reserve and bitcoin per share. Chief Executive Mike Ho said the company kept mining at a structural discount to spot and raised satoshis per share by about 5% without issuing shares through its at-the-market program or buying bitcoin on the open market. A paper gain carried American Bitcoin’s quarter The income statement makes the driver plain. American Bitcoin booked a $197.3 million gain on digital assets in the third quarter, after a $71.2 million loss on that line in the second. Operating income was about $191.8 million. Other expense included a $64.3 million loss on derivatives. Strip the mark-to-market move out of the picture and the operating story looks quieter. Revenue per bitcoin mined was about $71,100, down slightly from about $71,900 in the second quarter, and the cost to mine rose to about $42,100 from about $36,500, the company said. Production of about 891 bitcoin was below the second quarter’s roughly 932 coins, which the company had called its highest quarterly haul on record when it reported a $57.2 million second-quarter loss alongside a climb in holdings to about 8,002 BTC. American Bitcoin said it sold a portion of production to cover operating costs while still adding to its strategic reserve. Holdings rose by about 425 bitcoin, or about 5%, to roughly 8,427 as of Sept. 30. That total includes about 3,090 bitcoin pledged for miner purchases under agreements with Bitmain. Reserve up, satoshis per share up Management’s preferred yardstick is satoshis per share, which rose about 5% to roughly 11,572 from about 10,989 at the end of June. The share count reflects a 1-for-15 reverse stock split effected earlier this year on July 2. The owned fleet stood at about 89,242 bitcoin miners with roughly 28.1 EH/s of capacity at quarter-end. business.title: Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Judge Lets Stock Perpetual Futures Keep Trading but Says CFTC Likely Overstepped Its Authority Stock perpetual futures can keep trading on Kalshi, Coinbase Derivatives and Bitnomial for now after a federal judge denied an emergency bid to halt them Tuesday, while finding that the Wall Street-backed challengers are likely to prove the CFTC overstepped its authority. U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni denied the temporary restraining order on Nov. 3 after a teleconference with the parties, hours after the CFTC said the products could begin trading on U.S.-regulated exchanges. The plaintiff is the Capital Markets Alliance Association, a New York nonprofit whose members include Cboe Global Markets, Citadel Securities and the Healthy Markets Association, according to a declaration from its secretary, Adam Ford. The group sued the CFTC and Chairman Michael S. Selig in the Southern District of New York, case No. 1:26-cv-09608, seeking to undo the approvals of filings by all three exchanges. Caproni wrote that the group “is likely to succeed on the merits” of its claim that the agency lacks statutory authority to allow perpetual derivatives on individual stocks to be offered to retail investors on CFTC-regulated platforms. “Because the perpetual contracts, by definition, do not provide for a ‘sale for future delivery of a single security,’ they cannot be a security future over which the CFTC has statutory and regulatory authority,” she wrote. Instead, she said, the contracts “appear to satisfy the definition of a swap,” which falls to the Securities and Exchange Commission. She also found that the balance of equities and the public interest favor the alliance, writing that the agency’s actions “seem to represent a major disruption to the equities market.” The request failed on one prong. Caproni said the declarations from Cboe, Citadel Securities and Healthy Markets were “conjectural” about the harm members would suffer and did not show irreparable harm that was “actual and imminent.” What the ruling does and does not do The order leaves the approvals in place. It does not decide the case or the alliance’s separate motion for a preliminary injunction. The CFTC’s opposition is due Friday, Nov. 6, and the alliance’s reply is due Tuesday, Nov. 10. The order says that schedule is subject to change by the assigned judge. The docket lists Judge Lorna G. Schofield as assigned to the case. Kalshi was already listing four single-stock perps on Qualcomm, McDonald’s, Amgen and Costco by Wednesday morning, with maximum leverage of 4.9 times. Bloomberg Law reported that the judge signaled she might ultimately side with the Wall Street firms opposed to the products. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. entertainment.title: African Philanthropy Leaders Call for Bolder, Locally Led Giving at the 2026 APF Conference in Cape Town
entertainment.description: CAPE TOWN, South Africa: African Philanthropy Forum (APF) closed its 2026 Conference in Cape Town on 27 October with a message that ran through nearly every session: Africa’s challenges are connected, so African giving has to be connected too. Held from 25 to 27 October under the theme Bridge the Divide; Reimagine the Future , the conference brought together philanthropists, funders, business leaders, creatives, and technologists to ask how African capital can be mobilized, how partnerships can be strengthened, and how African-led solutions can be backed with more trust and flexibility. Centered on Africa, the program also looked outward, drawing on solutions from across the Global South and asking how African philanthropy can bridge the divide. The conference opened on Sunday evening with a reception at Cape Point Vineyards, where Executive Director Mosun Layode welcomed delegates, members and acknowledged APF Board members, including Chair Gbenga Oyebode , Wale Adeosun , and Nyimpini Mabunda . Former Board Member Phuthi Mahanyele-Dabengwa urged guests to look past the continent’s challenges and toward its potential and to use the days ahead to turn conversations into partnerships. It was an evening of connection before two days of ideas at the Norval Foundation. Reimagining the Future Monday, 26 October, began with a call to build bridges across regions, languages, and funding silos. Mosun Layode and Gbenga Oyebode officially opened and welcomed all delegates to the conference. Dr. Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka , former Vice President of South Africa, spoke of education as a sacred right of every African child and of bringing young people into decision-making. In the first keynote, Gary Lubner, Founder of the This Day Foundation, described giving away 95 percent of his wealth during his lifetime and said it was easier and more joyful than holding it for heirs. Old money thinking, he argued, is a major barrier to giving, and generosity includes time and effort as well as cash. The numbers framed the challenge. Delegates heard that Africa needs about $1.3 trillion in financing each year, while philanthropy contributes $5 billion to $6 billion. The task is to use that small pool to unlock far larger sources, such as pension funds and fixed-income assets, so money reaches businesses that create jobs. One retraining program they discussed moved 7,200 of 8,000 university graduates into tech jobs. The difference between charity and philanthropy, they said, is helping people help themselves. He told reporters Wednesday that Hall “fully deserves” the call-up after his performances in the previous window. He added that he did not hear Hall’s earlier comments about Poland, but that when Hall was with the team he “was really excited to play for us, for USA. That’s what is important.” The coach emphasized that commitment and performance matter more than past statements. The Rules of the Tie FIFA rules make the distinction clear for players under 21. An appearance in any official competition permanently ties a player to that national team, while friendlies alone do not. Hall has four senior caps so far, all in friendlies, so he is not yet locked in. The upcoming matches against Haiti count as official competition under CONCACAF and FIFA. Miami hosts the first match on Nov. 14, while the second occurs in Cincinnati on Nov. 17. If Hall plays in either of these, the door to Poland slams shut. sports.description: The Xavier boys soccer team has what seems like a pretty simple strategy. The Hawks figure if you don’t have the ball, you can’t score. sports.title: Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons gets brutally honest on expectations when he returns to play after ACL injury
sports.description: The Green Bay Packers are in last place in the NFC North despite having a 5-3 record. They have the best record of any last place team through eight weeks in the NFL since 1970, which is a testament to how well the division has played up to this point in the season. Truth be told, though, the Packers would be in a better position if they were not just 1-2 against their division opponents thus far in 2026. As the season hits its midway point and the weather becomes cold, Green Bay is going to be looking at making a run at a postseason spot. Fortunately, they will have All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons back soon, though he himself told fans to temper their expectations a little bit. Green Bay Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons needs to get back into game shape Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) during a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 12, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers defeated the Bengals 27-18. Parsons, of course, has not played yet this season as he continues to recover from the torn ACL he suffered late last year. When he first went down, the All-Pro prematurely predicted a September return. Now, we are in November and he has yet to play. This, however, is not because of any setbacks. The fact of the matter is that Parsons tore his meniscus as well. Furthermore, the Packers do not want him back on the field until he is 100% and has no risk of reinjuring that knee (remember what happened to David Bakhtiari?) While this is understood by most, it is easy to fall into the trap of thinking that Parsons will immediately be in mid-season form the second he steps onto the field for the first time. He himself told reporters that will not be the case. “I had a full lateral and medial meniscus repair, including the ACL, so when people are walking at three weeks, I’m still not weight bearing, so my quad is fully dead,” Parsons said . “I didn’t get off crutches until seven to eight weeks. So if you count that two months, I’m exactly where a nine-month (recovery) is supposed to be. So that’s why everyone’s timelines are different. I had a lot of damage done to my leg, and I think it’s a miracle that I’m even standing here today and opening up my window this early. “Am I going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person that I once was, this year? Probably not until later. I think you’ll see flashes of All-Pro Micah when I get to pass rush, and there’s gonna be times when you’re gonna be like, ‘Dang, what was Micah doing?’ There’s gonna be times that I question myself, too, like, ‘What was I doing right there?’… I’m not shying away from the possibility of my bad plays.” Fortunately, Green Bay’s pass rush has been better than many thought it would be without their All-Pro. Lukas Van Ness, Brenton Cox, Dani Dennis-Sutton, and others along the defensive front have picked up the slack and have the Packers tied for sixth in the NFL for most team sacks. sports.title: The one Portugal milestone Cristiano Ronaldo failed to reach as he announces retirement
sports.description: Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images Cristiano Ronaldo is arguably the greatest soccer player to ever play for Portugal and has helped the national team win three trophies during his 23-year career. Despite having helped the nation reach heights they were not used to reaching, Ronaldo fell short of one achievement, which he always wanted to achieve with Portugal, and that was making 250 appearances. As he announced his retirement today, Ronaldo walks away with 234 international appearances and 146 goals, the most by any player. The announcement comes just one month after he left the Portuguese football camp in September, following controversy with head coach Jorge Jesus. “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team,” Ronaldo said in an Instagram video. “Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone – they are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.” The Portuguese national team put out an official video on Instagram with a powerful caption that read: “A legacy that will live on forever. Thank you for everything, captain.” They also put out a statement to inform fans that a tribute was in the works for the legendary soccer player. “It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo’s immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much,” the statement read. Throughout his career, Ronaldo represented Portugal in six European Championships and won the competition once in 2016. He has also played in six World Cups and led the national team to the semi-finals in 2006. Ronaldo played in 178 competitive games and 56 friendlies throughout his career. 57 of his competitive appearances came in the World Cup and Euros. The 41-year-old has scored 25 goals in these games and helped his country become one of the leading nations in soccer. As he retires from international football, the country will now be without an icon who has carried the expectations of the Portuguese people for over two decades. Although many would say that his performances declined in the past few years, there was still an expectation of something big happening with him on the field. However, with the legend now having announced his retirement, the next generation of Portuguese talent will have to showcase that they are capable of taking the country to great heights. sports.title: Rare freshman starter Tommy Tofi settling in along Oregon football OL
sports.description: It's been a bumpy ride for Oregon football's first regular-season true freshman starter in the Dan Lanning era. From the onset, Tommy Tofi, at a massive 6-foot-6, 360 pounds, possessed the tools to succeed in his first year with the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten). Still, Lanning and offensive line coach A'lique Terry rarely go to first-year players along the interior. The only other first-year player to start for the Ducks under Lanning was current starting center Iapani Laloulu, who started the 2023 Fiesta Bowl only because Jackson Powers-Johnson opted out of the game. This is rare territory for an Oregon offensive lineman ahead of the Ducks ' biggest game of the season versus Ohio State. "It’s all been like kinda crazy," Tofi said. "Trying out different positions from left to right and just finding my rhythm." Tofi was used sparingly over the first month of the season and struggled with his assignments at times when he did get on the field. The freshman hasn't had trouble moving opposing players and creating gaps when he finds the right body, but the key has been being assignment sound. Since the second half against Nebraska on Oct. 17, Tofi has firmly held on to the left guard spot along the offensive line. He started his first game the week after against Illinois and played his best game of the season versus Northwestern last week. He said playing between Laloulu at center and veteran tackle Fox Crader has been instrumental to his success, along with his fair share of "cuss-outs." "A lot of cuss-outs from (Laloulu), (Douglas Utu) and a lot of the players," Tofi said with a smile when asked about how he's developed. "When you have four first-rounders on that D-line, that’s what helps you prepare and gets you ready for the season. Being able to go head-up with Matayo (Uiagalelei), Bear (Alexander), A’Mauri (Washington), Teitum (Tuioti), iron sharpens iron. You get better and better every day." Tofi has been part of a much-improved offensive line group that has stuck with a consistent group for the first time this season after rotating through different lineups over the first month and a half of the season. Ultimately, Lanning still wants to see more "strain" and effort from Tofi when the situation requires it. "Tommy is a guy that we’ve had a lot of confidence in from the beginning," Lanning said. "He’s got really good strength, got the ability to move people, which is huge. Now it’s about finding that extra strain. Can I strain from every play? I feel like every week that’s gotten a little better for Tommy." Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard. sports.title: EXCLUSIVE: Colonial Country Club likely losing PGA Tour event after 80-year run, per sources
sports.description: Colonial Country Club , home of the longest-running non-major event on the PGA Tour schedule, may not be hosting PGA Tour stars for much longer. Golfweek has learned that the Fort Worth, Texas-based private club, affectionately known as “Hogan’s Alley” for Ben Hogan’s five victories there, isn't expected to secure a place in the PGA Tour’s new Championship Series , which is scheduled to debut in 2028. Sources also say that the club likely will pass on an opportunity to participate in the Tour’s second-tier Challenger Series. Instead, Colonial, which currently hosts the Charles Schwab Challenge, could transition to PGA Tour Champions, and become the new home of the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, the season-ending playoff finale. The Tour previously said that final bids for the remaining four Championship Series events were due Sept. 30, and no decision has been made — an announcement will come at a later date. Sources say that only one tournament from the Dallas-Fort Worth area will be chosen for the Championship Series and CJ, the title sponsor for the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, has ponied up a better offer. It doesn't help that the footprint at Colonial is deemed to be maxed out and making it difficult to elevate the event the way the Tour would like to in order to generate additional revenue. More: PGA Tour overhauls competitive structure for 2028: How it works Officials view snub as 'insult' The club and Charles Schwab officials are still holding out hope that they will be selected for the Championship Series, but they are miffed that 80 years of loyalty and a sponsorship commitment that far exceeds most other companies is getting short shrift. Frustration is mounting for the club, and Schwab officials, that despite being an official marketing partner and a title sponsor on both tours, as well as the umbrella sponsor of both the season-long points race and postseason on PGA Tour Champions, they may be cast aside. They aren't thrilled with the prospect of hosting a Challenger Series event. One source said that club leadership termed being demoted after all these years as "an insult." Instead, they are believed to be weighing an offer to lean into the senior circuit and its familiar faces, many of whom are past champions and have a rich history at Colonial. The Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs consist of three events that determine the winner of the season-long title. The top 36 players in the standings following the Simmons Bank Championship advance to the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, where the player with the most cumulative points captures the Charles Schwab Cup and a share of a multimillion-dollar bonus pool. The playoff finale has been known as the Charles Schwab Cup Championship since 2003. It has been contested at Phoenix Country Club since 2017 after previously being held at Desert Mountain Club in Scottsdale, Arizona, starting in 2012. technology.title: Anthropic won't fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries
technology.description: A vulnerability in Anthropic’s Claude products lets any browser extension that can control Claude Dispatch make Claude Desktop run code on the computer – or even a different machine signed into the same Claude account – with no browser exploit and minimal user interaction required. Anthropic, aware of the problem since May, has taken no action to close the hole. Dispatch is a feature in Claude that lets users send and manage tasks from their mobile phone or browser to Claude Desktop, an AI agent that runs commands on their computer. Forever Security researcher Gal Weizman discovered that Claude Dispatch’s interface and API were reachable from an ordinary logged-in web session at claude.ai. So a browser extension able to control claude.ai could send commands to Claude Desktop as if they came from the legitimate Dispatch user. “That extension was able to perform a classic escalation of privileges. Because now Claude has access to the files in the operating system, it can run code on the operating system and compromise the machine completely,” said Weizman. “We’re talking about millions of installs.” Claude.ai received about 950 million monthly visits as of mid-2026, and Cowork usage included 1.2 million sampled sessions from more than 600,000 organizations during May, according to Anthropic’s usage data. Weizman found and disclosed the Claude Dispatch flaw, dubbed ThisBash, to Anthropic, and shared his research exclusively with The Register . The AI company acknowledged his report as a valid vulnerability in May, but closed the security issue as a duplicate of a known flaw it was already tracking. Anthropic did not pay Weizman a bug bounty or issue a CVE, but told him it planned to retire Dispatch at the end of October. That didn’t happen. The Claudefather did not respond to The Register ’s questions – including when it planned to retire the feature – but as of October 30, the official Claude support page listed Dispatch as available in limited beta on some Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, but not available to new users. “If you already use Dispatch, you can keep using it for now,” the page reads . Even if Anthropic does kill off Dispatch, Weizman says the fundamental flaw in Claude’s design still exists, and the security weakness now lives on in other features like Claude Code Remote Control and Claude Cowork sessions. technology.title: New York's Queens Public Library battles ransomware crims: Wi-Fi, checkouts, and website go dark
technology.description: New York City's Queens Public Library (QPL) is battling a ransomware attack, it confirmed on Wednesday evening via social media and to patrons directly. The disruption has downed QPL's website, on-site computers, check-out and return machines, its public Wi-Fi, mobile app, and its digital media services. Renewals are also unavailable, although library users are not charged fines for returning materials late. (Since 2021, In October 2021, QPL, Brooklyn Public Library, and New York Public Library - in an effort to help lower income users from being put off borrowing - permanently killed daily late fines on books and circulating materials .) Each of the library system's three branches remains open, including the central library in the Jamaica neighborhood in Queens, but QPL warned: "it will take some time before the library's network and systems are restored." QPL said "certain virtual and in-person programs may be impacted," advising visitors to check availability with their local branch via phone, and check the library's social media channels for official updates. "Our IT department is working to resolve the issue, and we will keep you informed,” it said in the statement. It added: "We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate your patience." No established ransomware group has yet claimed responsibility for the disruption, although attacks on publicly funded institutions rarely lead to lucrative payouts. The British Library's infamous ransomware attack in 2023 at the hands of Rhysida saw the organization refuse to pay the criminals' 20 Bitcoin ransom demand, opting instead to drain its cash reserves and fork out millions for an IT rebuild . Although the library's response to the attack drew widespread praise, few institutions of its kind are in a financial position to follow its lead. Other libraries might not be willing or able to commit to a recovery period as lengthy as that of the British Library . In its 2025/26 annual report , published in July, the institution said its recovery is still incomplete, and work to fully restore customers' ability to purchase electronic resources, such as journals and research databases, and reopen access to electronic legal deposit content is ongoing. This is likely to be completed by the end of 2026, the British Library added. ®

technology.title: Norway's aid agency pwned and all users' data is stolen
technology.description: Norway's national aid agency, Norad, has confirmed that cyber criminals broke into its systems, stealing information about each and every registered user of its grant portal. Norad, which coordinates Norway's assistance for foreign development, said that 20,614 registered individuals had their names and email addresses swiped, and information from at least three organizations' applications was "misdirected." The agency clarified that the grant portal, which was launched in 2017, has 20,614 registered users, meaning all were affected, across 12,511 organizations. In addition, the grant applications for at least three organizations are confirmed to be involved, though Norad said it may discover more as its investigation continues. Torger Kjeldstad, director of digitalization at Norad, said "the attack is complex," and confirmed the agency has initiated a crisis team to manage it. "We know a lot about what has happened, but to ensure that we have a complete overview of the attack, we are working to engage external experts in cybersecurity," he said. "They will give us a detailed description of what information those who attacked the solution have gained access to." Kjeldstad added that "it should be safe" to continue using Norad's services while it continues to probe what happened, and who was behind it. Norad did not reveal many details about how the attack unfolded, other than saying that 27 accounts were compromised and were then used to gain access to the portal and the data in question. The agency said the intrusion was detected on October 30, but did not offer any indication as to how long the attackers retained access to the grant portal. It also refused to rule out that names of applicants in "conflict areas and authoritarian states" may have been included in the stolen data – it is not known if recipients would have also been registered users – and said it is approaching the matter "very seriously." The grant portal, managed by Norad, which itself is part of Norway's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is responsible for handling applications from organizations across the world. Recent case studies include support for independent, investigative journalism in Moldova, a country which routinely battles Russian propaganda and election interference, and backing for Ukrainian children and prisoners of war. The issues Norad and the Norwegian government support, however, are wide-ranging – from access to healthcare for transgender people worldwide and Kenyan incubators for innovative transport solutions, to delivering aid to war-torn Gaza. ®

technology.title: SAP promises to open out data flows in both directions
technology.description: SAP has taken meaningful steps in opening its data to bidrectional sharing across the enterprise, and in decoupling the advanced analytics needed for AI from its ERP upgrade path. During a technical conference last week, the German software giant adopted native support for Apache Iceberg, the open table format, and extended its partnership with Databricks to bring data from legacy ERP systems into its modern cloud analytics platform. "By putting [a] stake in the ground with Iceberg, we now have SAP moving from a very closed application storage model to an open lakehouse model," said Aaron Rosenbaum, Gartner senior director analyst, referring to the concept which brings together data lakes and warehouses. Also important was the bridge between modern analytics in the cloud and on-prem or hosted legacy systems such as ECC, the ERP system broadly adopted by global companies. "SAP made a pretty big move in saying we're going to open this up, not just to S/4HANA Cloud [the latest ERP system], but ECC users. That coupling — leveraging of AI, leveraging a lakehouse for AI to the ERP upgrade lifecycle — was a problem," said Rosenbaum. In May this year, SAP bought Dremio, a lakehouse platform built around Apache Iceberg, ending its previous preference for Databricks' Delta Sharing to bring together SAP data products with existing lakehouses bi-directionally. At SAP's TedEd conference last week, SAP said its Business Data Cloud (BDC) – the "trusted data foundation for SAP Business AI Platform" – would now support native Apache Iceberg and a universal catalog powered by Apache Polaris, "providing an open and governed data foundation for users and [AI agent platform] Joule to consume data." Together with SAP BDC Connect, the new tech policy will support platform interoperability with "zero-copy data sharing" across platforms from Databricks, Snowflake, Google, AWS, and Microsoft. The system would also continue to support Delta Lake, the alternative open table format from Databricks, SAP said . With the integration of Dremio's SQL query engine, BDC users will also get access to relational databases including SQL Server, MongoDB, Oracle, and PostgreSQL without moving data, the vendor said. During the same conference, Databricks – the lakehouse company born out of an Apache Spark platform – extended its partnership with SAP based on the previously announced SAP Databricks, which embeds the Databricks Data + AI Platform in BDC. Outside of all the bombastic extravaganza of the Los Angeles launch, the first true AMG powered exclusively by batteries is a technological triumph that's as comfortable on the track as it is on the street. And it's really very good on the track. Triforce One of the fundamental problems with EVs is weight. Batteries are heavy, and the old rule about an object in motion tending to stay in motion makes the notion of nimble cornering a difficult engineering problem. Mercedes loves an engineering problem, and after two days behind the wheel of the AMG GT EV, the company has mostly reduced the battery-weight tax that mires EV performance.
